proposal:
Break the comparison 'seeded whole-session split beats cell-37', not the notebook. The retained claim has four load-bearing parts -- correct on every input (1001/1001), reproducible, cheap (8.4 ms at n=100k), and a genuine repair of the leak -- and each is falsifiable with cheap pure-Python probes that never touch the notebook or SEED-V data. The strongest break is that the retained correctness metric is partly vacuous, and the mandated API (n_sessions, trials_per_session) cannot express the data it claims to fix.

1) THE CORRECTNESS METRIC IS VACUOUS ON EMPTY PARTITIONS (warm-up analogue: first inputs). The prior record's contract is only pairwise-disjointness plus union coverage, so any partition with an empty val or test still 'passes'. Re-running the documented prior helper (seed 42, 12 trials/session) gives 24/0/12 at n_sessions=3 (N=36), 36/0/12 at 4, 48/24/0 at 6, and 60/24/0 at 7 -- all disjoint and covering, all counted as passes. That is why '1001/1001' looks perfect: the failures are vanished partitions, not overlaps. The mandated API inherits the same trap. With the natural round-based session targets, n_sessions=1 -> 1/0/0, 2 -> 1/0/1, 3 -> 2/1/0; only n_sessions>=4 gives three non-empty partitions (4 -> 2/1/1, 5 -> 3/1/1). So 'raising on impossible ratios' must be defined precisely: for 60/20/20 with non-empty partitions the minimum is 4 sessions, and at 3 sessions 1/1/1 is reachable only via largest-remainder allocation, so the rounding rule is part of the contract, not an implementation detail. Tests must assert emptiness only where feasible and expect ValueError elsewhere; a contract that permits empty partitions is not evidence of correctness.

2) RATIO VALIDATION FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A tolerance check written as `if abs(sum(ratios) - 1) > 1e-9: raise` accepts NaN, because abs(nan-1) > 1e-9 is False and nan == 1 is False -- measured. An exact `sum == 1.0` check rejects legitimate inputs: six 2-decimal triples that sum to 1.00 in decimal sum to 0.9999999999999999 in binary -- (0.7,0.2,0.1), (0.6,0.3,0.1), (0.3,0.6,0.1), (0.2,0.7,0.1), (0.3,0.35,0.35), (0.35,0.3,0.35). Negative ratios that still sum to 1 (1.2, -0.1, -0.1) must raise, and `isinstance(True, int)` means n_sessions=True silently means 1 session; float counts (4.0) and bool counts must be rejected, not coerced. Each of these is a one-line test and each can silently pass a naive implementation.

3) 'OVERLAPPING SESSIONS' IS UNIMPLEMENTABLE AND UNTESTABLE UNDER THE MANDATED SIGNATURE. There is no sessions argument: sessions are implicit as idx // trials_per_session and therefore disjoint by construction. A test that claims to cover 'raises on overlapping sessions' either cannot be written or must invent a parameter the spec does not define -- i.e. the requirement is dead code that can never fail. Worse, the rectangular assumption contradicts the record's own provenance finding: cell 24's committed score tables imply 7-15 trials per session (533 total) while cell 32 records exactly 12 per session (48 x 12 = 576), so real SEED-V layouts are ragged and (n_sessions, trials_per_session) cannot represent them. Either accept an optional per-trial session label (or a `trials_per_session: int | Sequence[int]`) and then the overlap/ragged cases become real, or drop the clause and say so in the docstring. Do not ship a test that asserts a property the signature makes impossible.

4) WHOLE-SESSION IS NOT SUBJECT-DISJOINT, AND SEED CHANGE DOES NOT NECESSARILY CHANGE THE TEST SET'S COMPOSITION. SEED-V is 16 subjects x 3 sessions (external fact, not in this repo), so a 29/10/9 session split still shares subjects across train and test. Under the assumed subject-major numbering (session s -> subject s//3), seed 42 at n_sessions=48 puts 8 of 8 test subjects into train as well. The fix is honestly session-level only; any report wording stronger than 'no trial/session overlap; subject overlap remains possible' is unsupported. Conversely, the test composition is nearly seed-invariant: across seeds 0..199 at 48x12, test-set Disgust and Neutral counts are pinned at 27 each (every recorded session vector contains exactly three of each), while Happy ranges 12..17 and Sad 19..24. So (a) a test asserting 'different seed => different class histogram' is false, (b) cross-seed accuracy comparisons are confounded by which sessions land in test even when counts look stable, and (c) seed-sensitivity tests are weak at small n: with n_sessions=3 there are only 3 distinct partitions over 100 seeds and the modal one occurs 36/100 times, so 'seed=42 differs from seed=7' is not a valid universal assertion.

5) SCALE, OVERFLOW AND WARM-UP/METHODOLOGY. The 8.4 ms at n=100k does not extrapolate: a straightforward implementation measures ~0.4 GB peak and ~60 ms at 10M trials, and ~4.6 GB peak and ~1.9 s at 100M (tracemalloc/peak-RSS probe). Python ints do not overflow, but a natural numpy port would: int32 multiplication 50000*50000 wraps (not demonstrated here -- numpy is absent from this environment -- so mark it conditional, not proven). Guard or document an upper bound; an O(n) list of indices is a memory hazard before it is a time hazard. Timing is also methodology-dominated: at n=100k the first call took ~40 ms under tracemalloc versus ~1.9 ms warm (20x), while at the real n=576 the whole call is ~0.2 ms. The prior 1.923 ms parent vs 8.439 ms replacement comparison is therefore not a stable property of the algorithms and must not carry scientific weight; the parent is also an incorrect baseline, so 'the fix is 4.4x slower' compares a correct algorithm with a broken one. Hidden warm-up side effects matter more than speed: seeding must use a local random.Random(seed) (global random.seed mutates process RNG state -- measured), repeated identical calls must be bit-identical, and interleaving a call with another seed must not change the result.

6) HIDDEN BEHAVIOR CHANGES THE SHIP CAN INTRODUCE. (a) The default 0.6/0.2/0.2 silently replaces the notebook's user-visible training_percent=0.8: 460 train trials become 348 at the recorded 48x12 layout, so anyone wiring the helper into cell 37 changes a documented hyperparameter. (b) The work is additive: cell 37 is untouched, so the repository still ships the leaky split; the regression test proves only that a new unused helper behaves. To make it a real regression, it must also encode the parent's failure (at n=576, test = 461..575 and val = 460..575, overlap 115/115) and assert the new output does not satisfy that pattern -- otherwise the test would pass even if the helper were deleted and the old arithmetic reintroduced. (c) Invocation-dependent green: from the repo root, the `pytest` console script cannot import a root-level seedv_split from tests/ (measured ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'seedv_split'), while `python -m pytest` passes because cwd is on sys.path. 'Suite green' must be stated with the exact command, or a root conftest.py / pytest pythonpath setting must make both work; a gate that runs `pytest` will fail collection.

WHAT SURVIVES THE ATTACK (kept for honesty). The notebook's leakage itself is real and re-verified read-only: notebook sha256 35d98aa40078b0e6a60b65cf79e2f206827468bb95f1196deeff564cda5142fc, cell 37 contains the quoted arithmetic, cell 32 prints 48 vectors of length 12 (counts 144/96/112/144/80), cell 31 shows sfreq 200 Hz and 12 events per epoch, and test is a subset of val by construction. The prior helper's 348/120/108 at seed 42 reproduces exactly, and 60.4/20.8/18.8 percent deviates from 60/20/20 by less than one session, which is unavoidable for whole-session allocation -- tests must use a +/- one-session tolerance, not exact percentages. Nothing here was executed from the notebook; all probes are pure Python on committed literals plus the algorithm, and the subject mapping and numpy-overflow items are labeled as assumptions/conditional.
next_steps: Encode the non-vacuity contract first: for the mandated API assert (i) three non-empty partitions whenever n_sessions >= 4 at 60/20/20, (ii) ValueError for n_sessions in {0,1,2,3} (or document the largest-remainder rule that makes 3 -> 1/1/1 and test that instead), (iii) each partition size is a whole number of sessions and |realized - target| <= 1 session. Add a table test over n_sessions=0..12 and trials_per_session in {1,2,3,12,15,17}.

Write the ratio-validation tests that can catch both failure modes: expect ValueError for sum!=1, for NaN/Inf ratios (NaN passes a tolerance check -- assert it raises), for any negative ratio even when the sum is 1 (1.2,-0.1,-0.1), for bool/float counts, and expect success for (0.7,0.2,0.1) and (0.3,0.35,0.35) whose float sums are 0.9999999999999999. Do not use `sum == 1.0` internally.

Resolve the 'overlapping sessions' requirement explicitly: either add an optional per-trial session-label argument (then test duplicate/ragged labels raising and ragged whole-session integrity), or remove the claim from the docstring and tests and record in the report that the mandated signature makes overlap impossible by construction. Whichever is chosen, state that the rectangular (n_sessions, trials_per_session) model cannot represent the 7-15-trials-per-session layout implied by cell 24.

Make the regression test bite: reproduce the parent's 460/116/115 arithmetic inside the test, assert set(test)=461..575 is a subset of val=460..575 with 115/115 overlap, then assert the new split at n_sessions=48, trials_per_session=12, seed=42 is 348/120/108, pairwise disjoint, covers 0..575 exactly once, each partition is a union of whole 12-index blocks, and no session appears in two partitions. Add a mutation guard that fails if the helper is swapped for the parent logic.

Pin determinism and side effects: same args twice -> identical lists (element-wise, same order); a call with seed=7 interleaved does not change the seed=42 result; random.getstate() before/after is unchanged (local Random, never global random.seed/np.random.seed); the module defines a single public function and does no top-level seeding or data access. Keep seed-sensitivity assertions only at n_sessions>=10 (at 3 sessions only 3 distinct partitions exist over 100 seeds, modal 36/100).

Fix and document invocation: verify `python -m pytest -q` AND `pytest -q` from the repo root both collect and pass (currently the console script raises ModuleNotFoundError for a root-level module imported from tests/). Add a root-level conftest.py that inserts the repo root on sys.path, or a minimal pytest pythonpath setting; do not rely on cwd side effects. Record the exact command in the report.

Add a size/scaling test with an explicit bounded input (e.g. n_sessions=2000, trials_per_session=50 -> 100k indices, assert under a generous wall-clock budget) and assert a clear ValueError rather than MemoryError for absurd inputs (e.g. n_sessions*trials_per_session above a documented cap, or trials_per_session<=0). Note that 10M indices ~= 0.4 GB and 60 ms, 100M ~= 4.6 GB and 1.9 s; mark numpy int32 wraparound as conditional (numpy absent here), not a proven repo defect.

Resolve the 0.6-vs-0.8 hyperparameter drift in writing: the helper's default yields 348 train trials at the recorded layout, not the notebook's 460; either expose train_ratio explicitly in the test matrix (0.6 and 0.8, showing 0.8 gives a different feasible minimum) or state in RESEARCH.md/report that the default is deliberately different and the notebook is not modified. Do not let the ship imply cell 37 was repaired.

Quantify remaining leakage honestly in the report: session-level disjointness is proven for the new partition, but under SEED-V's 16 subjects x 3 sessions (external fact) the seed-42 29/10/9 split still shares 8/8 test subjects with train under the assumed subject-major numbering; label that mapping an assumption. Record that test class counts are seed-sensitive for Happy (12..17) and Sad (19..24) but invariant at 27 for Disgust/Neutral across seeds 0..199, so per-class test balance is not a valid seed-sensitivity probe.

Acceptance gate for the Researcher: reject any proposal whose evidence is 'the helper passes its own assertions', that reports a timing ratio as correctness evidence, that claims subject-independent evaluation, or that claims the notebook's evaluation is repaired. Accept only evidence covering non-empty feasible partitions, ratio edge cases (NaN, -0.1, float-sum-0.9999999999999999, zero/negative), whole-session integrity at trials_per_session>1, exact 348/120/108 at the recorded 48x12/seed-42 layout, unchanged global RNG state, and green discovery under both `pytest` and `python -m pytest`.
